taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO as Aristolochia erecta L. The older Aristolochia repens Mill. is treated as a synonym.
look_here_first: Look low in grasses and open sandy ground. Swanflower is a tiny erect-to-sprawling perennial with very narrow grasslike leaves and a strange brown-purple curved flower arising near the stem. The showy tube is a petaloid fused calyx/perianth, not a normal petal corolla.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Aristolochiaceae herbarium index documents A. erecta as a Travis County species. Bexar — Bexar County Master Gardener field account documents a naturally occurring plant in dry sandy south Bexar County, found by following pipevine swallowtails. Kendall — a 2026 research-grade iNaturalist observation by peterjoseph is described as near Sisterdale; the Handbook of Texas places Sisterdale in Kendall County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: This is a mixed-source PASS. Travis is herbarium-grade; Bexar is a photographed direct field occurrence; Kendall is research-grade community science plus an independently verified locality-to-county mapping. Hays is explicitly NOT counted.

best_field_traits: small perennial herb, erect to sprawling, often hidden among grasses
flowers solitary in leaf axils on slender peduncles
petals absent; showy structure is a curved brown-purple fused petaloid calyx/perianth
perianth tube curved upward with a single strap-like limb
fruit an ovoid 5-valved capsule with many flat triangular seeds
morphology_keys.leaves: Narrow grasslike leaves are a major local gestalt cue but should not be used alone.
morphology_keys.flower: The brown-purple flower is built from a fused petaloid calyx/perianth, not a separate corolla. The curved tube and single limb are highly distinctive.
morphology_keys.ovary: Inferior; the compact gynostemium carries the anthers and styles in the flower center.
morphology_keys.fruit: Ovoid capsule opening by five valves; many flat triangular seeds.
morphology_keys.ecology: Central and South Texas sandy/open habitats; larval host for the pipevine swallowtail.

confused_with: grasses and narrow-leaved forbs when sterile
comparisons.key_distinctions: A. erecta is a tiny grass-mimic with narrow leaves and a brown-purple low flower; A. serpentaria is a taller woodland herb with broader variable leaves. Flower architecture confirms the genus.

photo_note: NPSOT/Lady Bird Johnson imagery and Bexar field photos are strong study references. Exact public-reuse local flower/ovary macros remain later visual polish.
